summary.text: A tidal bore is a wave formed by the leading edge of the incoming tide that travels up a river or narrow bay, against its current.
Bores occur in relatively few places, usually where a large tidal range is funneled from a broad bay into a shallow, narrowing river.
They bring intense turbulence and a rumbling roar, can be unsafe for shipping, and offer chances for river surfing.

facts.label: When it happens
facts.value: During the flood tide, never the ebb

facts.label: Surfing record
facts.value: 29 km up the Petitcodiac River in 2013

items.prompt: A river normally flows toward the sea, but one day a wall of water surges upstream. At what stage of the tide does this happen?

options.label: While the sea is falling
While the sea is rising
At slack water near low tide
At any stage, at random

items.explain: A tidal bore forms at the leading edge of the incoming tide and takes place during the flood tide, never the ebb.

items.prompt: Which place is most likely to have one of these upstream-rushing waves?

options.label: A deep, straight river on a coast with tiny tides
A lake with no connection to the sea
A wide, open beach facing the ocean
A shallow, narrowing river fed by a broad bay with big tides

items.explain: Bores usually form where a large tidal range is funneled from a broad bay into a shallow, narrowing river.

items.prompt: People can hear a big bore coming long before it arrives. Why does its sound carry so far?

options.label: Its rumble is low-pitched, which travels long distances
Its noise is a shrill hiss that cuts through the air
Its sound bounces back down off low clouds
It always arrives together with a thunderstorm

items.explain: The bore's rumble is heard far away because its low frequencies can travel over long distances.

items.prompt: Estuaries with bores are often rich in fish and shrimp. How does the bore itself help?

options.label: It warms the water as it moves upstream
It washes away the animals' predators
It mixes air into the water
It brings in fresh rainwater from inland

items.explain: The aeration caused by the tidal bore contributes to the abundant growth of many species of fish and shrimp.

items.prompt: A causeway was built across Canada's Petitcodiac River, and silt then piled up behind it. What happened to the river's bore?

options.label: It grew into the highest bore on Earth
It stayed just as it had been before
It moved over to a neighbouring river
It shrank to a ripple, then regrew once the gates opened

items.explain: Sedimentation after the causeway cut the bore to little more than a ripple; after the gates opened in 2010 it began to grow again.

items.prompt: Why does a funnel-shaped bay leading into a river matter for forming a bore?

options.label: It slows the incoming sea so it arrives gently
It raises the range and squeezes the rise into a sudden surge
It blocks most of the sea from entering the river
It turns the incoming seawater fresh

items.explain: The funnel shape increases the tidal range and can shorten the flood tide until it appears as a sudden rise in water level.
